cashTip: Cards work in towns; carry lei for villages, castles and parking. Tip about 10 percent.
name: Brașov
tagline: Saxon old town and the castles of Transylvania
summary: Brașov is a Saxon-built Transylvanian town under the forested Tâmpa mountain. Stroll the Council Square and the Gothic Black Church, ride the cable car to the Hollywood-style sign, and use the town as a base for Bran Castle (sold as Dracula's), the fairy-tale Peleș Castle, fortified Saxon churches and bear-watching in the Carpathians.
seasonNote: Summer for hiking and castles; the Christmas market and skiing at Poiana Brașov in winter.
arrival: Trains from Bucharest take 2.5 to 3 hours; Brașov airport has a few flights.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; trains to Sinaia, buses or a car for Bran and Râșnov.
foodTip: Sarmale (cabbage rolls) with polenta, papanași doughnuts, ciorbă soups and mici sausages.
buyTip: Local honey, țuică plum brandy and hand-painted ceramics.

items.name: Black Church
items.summary: Gothic church named for fire-blackened walls, with a huge collection of Ottoman carpets.
items.tip: Catch an organ concert in summer.

items.name: Council Square (Piața Sfatului)
items.summary: Pastel merchant houses around the old town hall.
items.tip: Sit at a café terrace in the evening.

items.name: Tâmpa Mountain
items.summary: Cable car or forest trail up to the Brașov sign and views over the town.
items.tip: Walk up, ride down.

items.name: Rope Street and Catherine's Gate
items.summary: One of Europe's narrowest streets, near the turreted medieval town gate.
items.tip: Walk on to the White and Black towers.

items.name: Bran Castle
items.summary: Hilltop castle marketed as Dracula's, with a royal history of its own.
items.tip: Go at opening; the story of Queen Marie is the real draw.

items.name: Peleș Castle
items.summary: Neo-Renaissance royal palace with lavish carved interiors in the mountains.
items.expect: Paid; closed Mondays and Tuesdays in some months.
items.tip: Take the train to Sinaia and walk up.

items.name: Râșnov Citadel
items.summary: Peasant fortress on a hilltop with walls and wide views.
items.tip: Combine with Bran on the same trip.

items.name: Prejmer fortified church
items.summary: UNESCO Saxon church inside a ring of thick walls with storage rooms for villagers.
items.tip: Climb into the defensive gallery.

items.name: Sarmale with polenta
items.summary: Pickled cabbage rolls of minced pork and rice with polenta and sour cream.
items.tip: Sergiana is a well-known traditional spot.

items.name: Papanași
items.summary: Fried cheese doughnuts with sour cream and berry jam.
items.tip: Share one after dinner.

items.name: Ciorbă soups
items.summary: Sour soups with tripe, beans or meatballs, often served in bread bowls.
items.tip: Try ciorbă de burtă with hot pepper.
flow: Order the soup of the day.

cashTip: Cards and phone payments work almost everywhere. Tip about 10 percent in restaurants.
name: Zakopane
tagline: Poland's mountain town at the foot of the Tatras
summary: Zakopane is Poland's winter capital and the gateway to the High Tatras. Hike to the glacial lake of Morskie Oko, ride the cable car to Kasprowy Wierch on the Slovak border, browse the smoked cheese stalls on Krupówki street and admire the wooden Zakopane-style houses. Skiing in winter, hut-to-hut hiking in summer.
seasonNote: Summer for hiking, January to March for skiing; weekends are very busy.
arrival: Buses and trains from Kraków take about 2 to 2.5 hours.
gettingAround: Minibuses to trailheads; walk the town.
foodTip: Oscypek smoked sheep cheese grilled with cranberry, kwaśnica sour cabbage soup and pierogi.
buyTip: Oscypek cheese and wool from the Gubałówka market.

items.name: Morskie Oko
items.summary: Emerald lake under granite peaks, reached by a 9 km paved road walk or horse cart.
items.expect: Park fee; very busy; book parking online.
items.tip: Continue up to Czarny Staw for fewer people.

items.name: Kasprowy Wierch cable car
items.summary: Cable car to a 1,987 m summit on the Polish-Slovak border.
items.expect: Paid; book tickets online in season.
items.tip: Walk the ridge a little on a clear day.

items.name: Gubałówka
items.summary: Funicular to a hill with a market and a classic panorama of the Tatras.
items.tip: Ride up for sunset.

items.name: Krupówki Street
items.summary: Main pedestrian street with wooden inns, stalls and street music.
items.tip: Look for highland folk bands in the evening.

items.name: Villa Koliba and Zakopane style
items.summary: The first wooden house in the Zakopane style, now a museum.
items.tip: Walk on to the old wooden church on Kościeliska.

items.name: Dolina Kościeliska
items.summary: Gentle valley walk to caves and a mountain hut.
items.tip: Bring a torch for Mroźna Cave.

items.name: Chochołowskie Termy
items.summary: Big thermal pools with mountain views.
items.tip: Go after a hiking day.

items.name: Grilled oscypek
items.summary: Smoked sheep cheese grilled and served with cranberry jam from street stalls.
items.expect: Look for the protected oscypek label.
items.tip: Buy from highlanders at the market.

items.name: Highland karczma
items.summary: Wooden inns serving kwaśnica, roast lamb and pierogi with live highland music.
items.tip: Order kwaśnica and placki po góralsku.

items.name: Mountain hut meal
items.summary: Schronisko huts serve soup, pierogi and szarlotka to hikers.
items.tip: Try szarlotka apple cake.

cashTip: Cards and phone payments work almost everywhere. Tip about 10 percent in restaurants.
name: Wrocław
tagline: Islands, bridges and hundreds of bronze dwarfs
summary: Wrocław is a city of islands and bridges on the Oder, with one of Europe's finest market squares. Hunt for the 600 tiny bronze dwarfs hidden around town, see the lamplighter on Ostrów Tumski at dusk, walk into the 114 m Racławice Panorama painting and climb the cathedral towers.
seasonNote: Summer is lively; the Christmas market is one of Poland's best.
arrival: Trains from Kraków take 3 hours, from Berlin about 4h30; the airport is 30 minutes by bus.
gettingAround: Walk the centre; trams for the rest.
foodTip: Pierogi, żurek sour rye soup in bread, and craft beer from Świdnicka Cellar.

items.name: Market Square (Rynek)
items.summary: Huge square of painted houses around the Gothic Old Town Hall.
items.tip: Look at the town hall's astronomical clock face.

items.name: Ostrów Tumski
items.summary: Oldest part of town with the cathedral and gas lamps lit by hand each dusk.
items.tip: Arrive at dusk to see the lamplighter.

items.name: Racławice Panorama
items.summary: Giant 360° painting of a 1794 battle, viewed from a central platform.
items.tip: Book a slot online.

items.name: Wrocław dwarfs hunt
items.summary: Hundreds of bronze dwarf figures hidden on pavements and walls.
items.tip: Get a dwarf map from the tourist office.

items.name: University of Wrocław Aula Leopoldina
items.summary: Baroque university hall and the Mathematical Tower with a rooftop view.
items.tip: Climb the tower after the hall.

items.name: Centennial Hall and Japanese Garden
items.summary: UNESCO-listed concrete dome of 1913, with a fountain show and Japanese garden nearby.
items.tip: Evening fountain shows in summer.

items.name: Hala Targowa
items.summary: 1908 market hall with produce, pickles and cheap lunch counters.
items.tip: Grab pierogi at a counter.

items.name: Pierogi
items.summary: Dumplings filled with potato and cheese, meat or seasonal fruit.
items.tip: Pierogarnia Stary Młyn on the Rynek is popular.

items.name: Żurek in bread
items.summary: Sour rye soup with sausage and egg, served in a hollowed bread loaf.
items.tip: Good on a cold day.

items.name: Piwnica Świdnicka
items.summary: One of Europe's oldest restaurants, in the cellars of the town hall.
items.tip: Have a beer under the vaults.

cashTip: Cards work everywhere, even for tiny sums. Tipping is not expected.
name: Rovaniemi
tagline: Northern lights, huskies and Santa on the Arctic Circle
summary: Rovaniemi is the capital of Finnish Lapland, right on the Arctic Circle. Cross the line at Santa Claus Village, ride a husky or reindeer sled through snowy forest, hunt the northern lights from August to April, learn about the Arctic at Arktikum, and come back in summer for the midnight sun.
seasonNote: Northern lights from late August to early April; polar night in December; midnight sun in June and July.
arrival: Flights from Helsinki take 1h15; the overnight Santa Claus Express train takes about 10 to 12 hours.
gettingAround: Buses to Santa Claus Village; tours include pickups.
foodTip: Sautéed reindeer with lingonberries and mash, salmon soup and leipäjuusto squeaky cheese with cloudberry jam.
buyTip: Sámi crafts, Marimekko and Moomin goods, and Lappish leather.

connections.note: Several flights a day; or the overnight train.

items.name: Santa Claus Village
items.summary: Meet Santa every day of the year and cross the painted Arctic Circle line.
items.expect: Free to enter; photos with Santa cost money.
items.tip: Send a postcard from Santa's Main Post Office.

items.name: Husky safari
items.summary: Mush your own team of huskies through snowy forest.
items.tip: Choose a farm with longer rides and small groups.

items.name: Northern lights hunt
items.summary: Drive away from city lights to watch the aurora borealis.
items.tip: Check the aurora forecast and cloud cover.

items.name: Arktikum
items.summary: Museum of Arctic nature and Sámi life under a long glass tube.
items.tip: Watch the aurora film inside.

items.name: Reindeer farm
items.summary: Visit a family farm and ride a reindeer sleigh.
items.tip: Ask about reindeer herding life.

items.name: Ounasvaara hill
items.summary: Ski hill and summer hiking trails with a view over the river and town.
items.tip: Midnight sun view in summer.

items.name: Korundi House of Culture
items.summary: Art museum and concert hall in an old brick post-bus depot.
items.tip: Check for a Lapland Chamber Orchestra concert.

items.name: Sautéed reindeer
items.summary: Thin-sliced reindeer cooked in butter with mashed potatoes and lingonberries.
items.tip: Nili is a known Lappish restaurant.

items.name: Salmon soup
items.summary: Creamy salmon and potato soup with dill and rye bread.
items.tip: Try a lunch buffet for good value.

items.name: Leipäjuusto with cloudberries
items.summary: Warm squeaky bread-cheese served with cloudberry jam.
items.tip: Have it with coffee.

cashTip: The Faroese króna is on a par with the Danish krone, and cards work everywhere. Tipping is not expected.
name: Faroe Islands
tagline: Sheer cliffs, grass-roofed villages and sea-level waterfalls
summary: The Faroe Islands are 18 rugged islands in the North Atlantic between Iceland and Norway. Photograph the Múlafossur waterfall dropping into the sea at Gásadalur, hike to the lake that hangs above the ocean at Sørvágsvatn, take the ferry to Mykines for puffins, and stay in Tórshavn, one of the world's smallest capitals.
seasonNote: May to August for long days and puffins (Mykines, roughly May to August); weather changes fast all year.
arrival: Flights from Copenhagen take 2 hours; Vágar Airport is 45 minutes from Tórshavn by tunnel.
gettingAround: Rent a car; undersea tunnels link the main islands (some tolled), ferries and helicopters reach the rest.
foodTip: Fermented ræst lamb and fish, fresh langoustines and Faroese salmon.

items.name: Múlafossur waterfall, Gásadalur
items.summary: Waterfall plunging off a cliff into the ocean below a tiny village.
items.expect: Close to the airport; viewpoint is free.
items.tip: Go in the evening light.

items.name: Sørvágsvatn (Lake above the ocean)
items.summary: Hike along the lake to the Trælanípa cliff for the illusion of a lake floating above the sea.
items.tip: Allow 3 hours return.

items.name: Mykines
items.summary: Remote island with puffin colonies and a lighthouse walk.
items.expect: Ferry or helicopter; hiking fee; guide sometimes required.
items.tip: Book the ferry early; check the weather.

items.name: Tórshavn old town (Tinganes)
items.summary: Turf-roofed red houses on the rock where one of the world's oldest parliaments met.
items.tip: Walk around the harbour at sunset.

items.name: Saksun
items.summary: Grass-roofed church and farms above a tidal lagoon.
items.tip: Walk to the lagoon at low tide.

items.name: Gjógv
items.summary: Village beside a deep sea gorge used as a natural harbour.
items.tip: Have waffles at the guesthouse.

items.name: Kirkjubøur
items.summary: Medieval church ruins and a farmhouse lived in by the same family for 17 generations.
items.tip: Combine with a Tórshavn day.

items.name: Ræst food
items.summary: Fermented wind-dried lamb and fish, the islands' oldest taste.
items.tip: Raest restaurant in Tórshavn serves a whole menu of it.

items.name: Langoustines and seafood
items.summary: Fresh Faroese langoustines, cod and salmon.
items.tip: Look for harbour-front restaurants.

items.name: Heimablídni home dining
items.summary: Dinner in a Faroese family's home, a local tradition.
items.tip: Ask the tourist office for hosts.

cashTip: Cards are widely accepted, but carry cash for tavernas, kiosks and beach loungers. Tip 5 to 10 percent.
name: Naxos
tagline: The Cycladic island of beaches, marble villages and the Portara
summary: Naxos is the biggest Cycladic island and the greenest, with long sandy beaches and mountain villages. Watch sunset through the giant marble Portara gate, get lost in the Venetian castle lanes of Chora, swim at Plaka and Agios Prokopios, and drive inland to Halki, Apeiranthos and the Temple of Demeter.
seasonNote: June and September are warm and calmer; August is busy and windy with the meltemi.
arrival: Ferries from Piraeus take 3.5 to 6 hours; short flights from Athens.
gettingAround: Buses link Chora and the beaches; rent a car or quad for the villages.
foodTip: Naxos potatoes, graviera and arseniko cheeses, kitron liqueur and local meats.

items.name: Portara
items.summary: Huge marble doorway of an unfinished temple to Apollo on an islet by the harbour.
items.tip: Come early for sunset or watch from the causeway.

items.name: Chora old town and Kastro
items.summary: Whitewashed lanes climbing to a 13th-century Venetian castle quarter.
items.tip: Visit the archaeological museum inside the Kastro.

items.name: Plaka and Agios Prokopios beaches
items.summary: Long golden beaches with clear water and dunes.
items.tip: Walk south along Plaka for quiet spots.

items.name: Halki and the Tragea valley
items.summary: Old capital among olive groves, with the Vallindras kitron distillery.
items.tip: Taste kitron at the distillery.

items.name: Apeiranthos
items.summary: Marble-paved mountain village with small museums.
items.tip: Have lunch on the main lane.

items.name: Temple of Demeter
items.summary: Restored 6th-century BC marble temple in farmland.
items.tip: Combine with Halki.

items.name: Kouros of Apollonas
items.summary: Giant 10 m unfinished marble statue lying in an ancient quarry.
items.tip: Drive the north coast road.

items.name: Naxian taverna
items.summary: Grilled local meats, Naxos potatoes and graviera cheese.
items.tip: Order the local beef and fried graviera.

items.name: Seafront fish tavernas
items.summary: Fresh grilled fish and octopus by the water.
items.tip: Ask the price before ordering.

items.name: Kitron liqueur
items.summary: Sweet liqueur made from citron leaves, only on Naxos.
items.tip: Taste green, yellow and clear.

cashTip: Cards are widely accepted, but carry cash for tavernas, kiosks and beach loungers. Tip 5 to 10 percent.
name: Zakynthos
tagline: Shipwreck Beach, sea caves and loggerhead turtles
summary: Zakynthos is an Ionian island of white cliffs and electric-blue water. See the famous Shipwreck Beach of Navagio from the cliff-top viewpoint or by boat, swim inside the Blue Caves, spot loggerhead turtles in Laganas Bay, and taste the island's Venetian-era food and music in the villages.
seasonNote: June and September are ideal; Laganas is party-busy in July and August.
arrival: Direct summer flights from much of Europe; ferries from Kyllini on the mainland take 1 hour.
gettingAround: Rent a car or scooter; boat trips for Navagio and the caves.
foodTip: Sartsa beef stew, ladotyri cheese, mandolato nougat and Verdea wine.
buyTip: Mandolato nougat and local olive oil.

connections.note: Daily flights; or bus and ferry via Kyllini.

items.name: Navagio (Shipwreck Beach)
items.summary: Rusting shipwreck on a white cove under sheer cliffs.
items.expect: Landing on the beach is often banned after rockfalls; check before booking.
items.tip: See it from the cliff viewpoint in the morning.

items.name: Blue Caves
items.summary: Sea caves where sunlight turns the water glowing blue.
items.expect: Small boats from Agios Nikolaos or Skinari.
items.tip: Go before 11 am for the best light.

items.name: Marathonisi (Turtle Island)
items.summary: Island in the marine park where loggerhead turtles nest.
items.tip: Choose a turtle-friendly licensed boat.

items.name: Keri cliffs and lighthouse
items.summary: Cliff-top lighthouse with arches in the sea below.
items.tip: Have a drink at the café at sunset.

items.name: Zakynthos Town and Bochali
items.summary: Arcaded town rebuilt after the 1953 quake, with the Venetian castle hill of Bochali above.
items.tip: Have dinner at Bochali for the view.

items.name: Porto Limnionas
items.summary: Rocky inlet with turquoise water for swimming off the rocks.
items.tip: Bring water shoes.

items.name: Sartsa and island stews
items.summary: Beef braised with tomato, garlic and cheese, a Zakynthian speciality.
items.tip: Ask for local dishes, not the tourist menu.

items.name: Kantades dinner
items.summary: Tavernas where singers perform kantades, Venetian-style serenades.
items.tip: Ask locals where kantades play tonight.

items.name: Mandolato nougat
items.summary: Soft white almond nougat, a Zakynthos sweet.
items.tip: Buy from a family workshop.
